quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal Q2 2026 (quarter ended December 26, 2025) revenue was a record $1.13 billion, up 36% year over year - the fastest year-over-year growth since the IPO over fifteen years ago - and up 16% from Q1, above the guidance range. Non-GAAP EPS was a record $3.36, above guidance despite a $3 million (9¢ per share) FX revaluation loss. Non-GAAP gross margin was 12.4% (up 10 basis points from Q1, flat year over year despite FX headwinds) and operating margin reached 10.9% (up 30 basis points from both Q1 and a year ago); net income was $122 million. Cash and short-term investments ended at $961 million; operating cash flow was $46 million and free cash flow an outflow of $5 million (CEO Seamus Grady and CFO Csaba Sverha).
quarterly_data.figure: Revenue $1.13 billion (record; +36% YoY, +16% QoQ); non-GAAP EPS $3.36 incl. $3 million (9¢) FX loss; gross margin 12.4%; operating margin 10.9%; net income $122 million; cash + short-term investments $961 million; operating cash flow $46 million; free cash flow outflow $5 million

quarterly_data.signal: Optical communications revenue was $833 million, up 29% year over year and 11% from Q1. Within it, telecom revenue was a record $554 million (up 59% year over year, 17% from Q1); data center interconnect (DCI) module revenue was $142 million (up 42% year over year, 3% from Q1); datacom revenue was $278 million, down 7% year over year but up 2% sequentially, with trends 'favorable for continued sequential growth'.
quarterly_data.figure: Optical comms $833 million (+29% YoY, +11% QoQ); telecom $554 million (record; +59% YoY, +17% QoQ); DCI modules $142 million (+42% YoY, +3% QoQ); datacom $278 million (down 7% YoY, up 2% QoQ)

quarterly_data.signal: Non-optical communications revenue was $300 million, up 61% year over year and 30% from Q1, driven primarily by high-performance computing (HPC) products at $86 million versus $15 million in Q1 (the first quarter the category was broken out). Automotive revenue was $117 million, up 12% year over year but slightly down sequentially as anticipated; industrial laser revenue was $41 million, up 10% year over year and 4% sequentially.
quarterly_data.figure: Non-optical comms $300 million (+61% YoY, +30% QoQ); HPC $86 million (vs $15 million in Q1); automotive $117 million (+12% YoY); industrial laser $41 million (+10% YoY, +4% QoQ)

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 FY2026 guidance: revenue of $1.15 billion to $1.2 billion (approximately 35% year-over-year growth at the midpoint) and non-GAAP EPS of $3.45 to $3.60 (approximately 40% growth at the midpoint). Sequential growth expected in telecom, datacom and HPC, with another modest sequential decline in automotive. CFO: HPC will not repeat last quarter's 'nice bump of about $71 million sequentially' but double-digit growth is anticipated; DCI is expected to grow faster than in Q2; based on the hedging program, FX is expected to be about a 20 to 30 basis point gross margin headwind, to be offset mostly through operating leverage.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 FY2026 guide: revenue $1.15 billion-$1.2 billion (approximately 35% YoY at midpoint); non-GAAP EPS $3.45 to $3.60 (approximately 40% YoY); HPC double-digit growth after about $71 million QoQ bump; FX gross margin headwind about 20 to 30 basis point

quarterly_data.signal: Datacom remained supply constrained, 'particularly on the leading-edge products at 200 gig per lane, both 800 gig and 1.6'. Demand continues to outstrip supply and Fabrinet continues to ship significant volumes to its main customer but 'could ship more if we had more components'. The EML laser has been the main cause of the constraint; the customer approved a 'second source for the EML for the laser' during the quarter, which should benefit Q3 and future quarters - management says it is 'starting to see that resolution come through now'. Datacom output is almost all 200 gig per lane (1.6 terabits and 800 gig, built on the same production line); the 800G/1.6T mix is the customer's decision and not important to Fabrinet.
quarterly_data.figure: 200 gig per lane (800 gig and 1.6 terabits) supply-constrained by EML lasers; second EML source approved in the quarter

quarterly_data.signal: DCI and telecom demand color: DCI is mostly 400 ZR and 800 ZR modules; the next-generation 800 ZR products are 'yet to ramp'. Fabrinet says it has 'all of the market-leading customers in the space' and believes long-term DCI demand is durable. Reported DCI revenue covers only coherent modules with high confidence of DCI use (400 and 800 ZR modules and variants plus some embedded coherent line card modules), not telecom systems. Telecom growth was particularly strong as Fabrinet 'started to ramp, you know, Sienna's new system program' (name as transcribed) plus other new program wins, still early; management agreed the telecom growth was 'predominantly DCI' and 'not just Sienna, it is across multiple customers'. Satellite communications has been growing steadily (not broken out) and the complete network systems business continues to grow.
quarterly_data.figure: DCI mostly 400 ZR and 800 ZR modules; next-generation 800 ZR yet to ramp

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Seamus Grady: co-packaged optics is an evolution of Fabrinet's silicon photonics and precision photonics packaging capabilities and is 'much more real than it has ever been'. Fabrinet believes it is far ahead of most competitors, is already seeing some CPO revenue (relatively small right now) and is 'working on co-packaged optics programs with three different customers'; timing of material revenue depends on customers' roadmaps and schedules. Fabrinet is 'in the ecosystem' of the CPO switch supply chain but declined to detail its CPO switch work.
quarterly_data.figure: CPO programs with three different customers; CPO revenue relatively small

quarterly_data.signal: Optical circuit switching (OCS): Fabrinet is 'engaged on a number of fronts' in what is 'a completely new product category', working on a couple of projects in the space with nothing to announce; revenue timing depends on customers' ramp schedules, and management thinks OCS 'has a significant role to play in the future'.

Datacom diversification: Fabrinet has several projects under way both with hyperscalers directly (producing transceivers for hyperscalers) and with merchant transceiver manufacturers, nothing to announce yet. It has been working on this for 'well over a year, probably eighteen months' and is 'quarters away rather than years away' from meaningful revenue. Management also cited additional high-performance compute customers and additional CPO as growth drivers, and stressed it is a pure contract manufacturer with no products of its own.
quarterly_data.figure: hyperscale-direct and merchant transceiver programs quarters away rather than years away from meaningful revenue

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity: Building 10 at the Chonburi campus (2 million square feet) is on track, with about 250,000 square feet finished and ready by June - pulled in 'six, eight months ahead of the original schedule' for several customers across telecom (DCI and new telecom wins) and datacom - and possession of the balance expected around January 2027. On Building 10 capacity: 'we said 2.5 in the past is probably a little bit north of that at the moment given the mix'. At Pinehurst, about 120,000 square feet of office and warehouse space is being converted to manufacturing now, which 'should give us over $150 million revenue upside opportunity' (mix-dependent). Building 8 (550,000 square feet) filled quickly, Building 9 (1 million square feet) is almost full, and there is room for Buildings 11 and 12 on the same campus. Q2 capital expenditures were $52 million, above maintenance levels, for Building 10 and Pinehurst.
quarterly_data.figure: Building 10: about 250,000 square feet by June, six, eight months ahead of the original schedule; capacity 'we said 2.5 in the past', now 'a little bit north'; Pinehurst about 120,000 square feet -> over $150 million revenue upside; Q2 CapEx $52 million

connects_to.relationship: high-performance computing (HPC) program manufacturing for AWS custom silicon platforms

contracts.signal: Fabrinet's first HPC program contributed $86 million in Q2 (versus $15 million in Q1) and is running on two fully automated production lines with additional lines being qualified. CEO Seamus Grady said the ramp is 'a little more than halfway' and the company expects 'the revenue from our current HPC program to be north of about $150 million when it is fully ramped', reached over the next couple of quarters. Fabrinet is pursuing other HPC customers 'as our relationship with AWS is not exclusive', and 'we are currently a second source in that program' - by beating the customer's cost, quality and delivery expectations it may earn a larger share; the incumbent is 'a very good supplier with a long relationship with the customer'. Multiple products (current and new) are ramping with the customer.
contracts.value: $86 million HPC revenue in Q2; north of about $150 million when fully ramped
contracts.type: contract manufacturing (HPC program ramp, second source)
